name: Moses at the waters of Meribah
charge: Failing to sanctify the Lord before the people: must we fetch you water out of this rock?
summary: There was no water, and the people chode with Moses, loud and angry, wishing they had died when their brethren died. Moses had to deal with all twelve tribes at once, and a stomach can only take so much of a rebellious people. Told to speak to the rock, he called them rebels, asked whether he and Aaron must fetch them water out of this rock, and smote it twice. That we is how the record shows he was out of the spirit: he put himself in the place of the One giving the water. The water still came, and the sentence with it.
offenseFull: The congregation came into the desert of Zin in the first month and abode in Kadesh, and Miriam died there and was buried there (Numbers 20:1). There was no water for the congregation, and they gathered together against Moses and against Aaron. The people chode with Moses, which is to say they raised their voices in a loud, angry, shouting argument: they wished they had died when their brethren died before the Lord, and asked why they had been made to come up out of Egypt into this evil place, with no seed, figs, vines or pomegranates, and no water to drink (Numbers 20:2-5). Taken out of Egypt by the hand of the Most High and headed to the promised land, they forgot so quickly how they were brought out, and anything out of the ordinary they complained about. Moses had to deal with twelve tribes at once, twelve personalities and twelve attitudes, and that brother deserves all the honour he is given.

The command was exact: take the rod, gather the assembly with Aaron, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it would give forth its water for the congregation and their beasts (Numbers 20:7-8). At this point Moses got out of the spirit; a stomach can only take so much of a rebellious people. He called them rebels and asked, must we fetch you water out of this rock? The Lord never told him to say that. That we is how you know he was off: he put himself alongside the One who was giving the water. Then he lifted up his hand and struck the rock twice with his rod (Numbers 20:9-11). The psalm gives the cause: they provoked his spirit, so that he spoke unadvisedly with his lips (Psalms 106:32-33). Anger is what clouds a man’s judgment; it takes him out of the spirit, and then he leans on his own understanding instead of trusting the Lord with all his heart and keeping to the instruction he was given (Proverbs 3:5). A wrathful man stirs up strife, but the man slow to anger appeases it (Proverbs 15:18).
judgmentFull: The water came out abundantly, and the congregation and their beasts drank; the people lost nothing by it (Numbers 20:11). The Lord told Moses and Aaron that because they had not believed Him, to sanctify Him in the eyes of the children of Israel, they would not bring this congregation into the land He had given them (Numbers 20:12-13). This is the water of Meribah, which means strife, because the children of Israel strove with the Lord, and He was sanctified in them. Set beside it the war with Og a short time later, when the people said that the Lord their God delivered the king of Bashan into their hands (Deuteronomy 3:3): they were doing the fighting, and they gave the praise, the glory and the victory to the Most High, and did not boast in their own swords. That is what sanctifying Him looks like, and at the rock Moses did the opposite.

Forty years of carrying the nation ended with the two men kept out of the land for a sentence spoken out of the spirit. At mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, the Lord said Aaron would be gathered to his people because they had rebelled against His word at the water of Meribah; Moses stripped him of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there on the top of the mount, and all the house of Israel mourned him thirty days (Numbers 20:23-29). Moses was told to go up into mount Abarim and see the land, and then be gathered to his people as Aaron was, for the same cause (Numbers 27:12-14). He begged to go over and see the good land beyond Jordan, and the answer was final: let it suffice, and speak no more of this matter (Deuteronomy 3:23-26), the way a parent tells a child who keeps asking that the matter is closed. His charge was to strengthen and encourage the man appointed to take the people over in his place.

text.text: Then came the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, into the desert of Zin in the first month: and the people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.
And there was no water for the congregation: and they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron.
And the people chode with Moses, and spake, saying, Would God that we had died when our brethren died before the Lord!
And why have ye brought up the congregation of the Lord into this wilderness, that we and our cattle should die there?
And wherefore have ye made us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us in unto this evil place? it is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink.
And Moses took the rod from before the Lord, as he commanded him.
And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?
And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.
They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes:
Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.

And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.
This is the water of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with the Lord, and he was sanctified in them.
So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.
And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron in mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, saying,
Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah.
Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up unto mount Hor:
And strip Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son: and Aaron shall be gathered unto his people, and shall die there.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded: and they went up into mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.
And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there in the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount.
And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they mourned for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Get thee up into this mount Abarim, and see the land which I have given unto the children of Israel.
And when thou hast seen it, thou also shalt be gathered unto thy people, as Aaron thy brother was gathered.

For ye rebelled against my commandment in the desert of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify me at the water before their eyes: that is the water of Meribah in Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.
And I besought the Lord at that time, saying,
O Lord God, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might?
I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.
But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me: and the Lord said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.
